categoryRules.description: First matching rule wins. Test runners, routing, setup, inventories, affected selection, coverage, and build-budget policy.
First matching rule wins. Mounted and browser-shaped ChatScreens behavior is visible chat/UI evidence, even when it invokes generation.
First matching rule wins. Settings, provider panels, Realm/catalog, and plugin/module authoring UI stay in the authoring category.
First matching rule wins. Authentication, authorization, egress and body limits, tracing, startup/shutdown, service workers, and platform routes.
First matching rule wins. Asset bytes and ownership, imports/exports, saves, backups, archive codecs, Realm staging, and historical formats.
First matching rule wins. Plugin/module permissions and lifecycle, MCP, RisuAccess, Playground, and developer-specialized tools.
First matching rule wins. CBS, parsing, regex/display scripts, triggers, Lua, automation, and bounded execution.
First matching rule wins. Memory, embeddings, summaries, ranking, jobs, queues, and worker lifecycle.
First matching rule wins. Provider adapters, models and credentials, translation, image/audio/transcription, and media codecs.
First matching rule wins. Prompt assembly, generation operations and effects, streaming, finalization, reroll, and Agent Presets.
First matching rule wins. Browser bootstrap, writer/observer state, outbox/replay, hydration, invalidation, refresh, and recovery.
First matching rule wins. SQLite persistence, revisions and receipts, commands/events, durable mutations, repositories, and editing bridges.
First matching rule wins. Settings UI, profiles, personas, characters, lorebook authoring, catalogs, loadouts, and reordering.
First matching rule wins. Navigation, visible chat behavior, sidebars, shared UI feedback, focus, accessibility, and responsive behavior.
A path unmatched above uses D when its resolved lane is built-browser or frontend-dom.
A path unmatched above uses L when its resolved lane is fastify-node.
Any remaining tracked frontend N/S path uses A and remains explicitly visible for Phase 1 review.

audit.risk: High browser bundle breakage or an unenforced shared-protocol architecture boundary.
audit.companionEvidence: package exports and TypeScript protocol build constrain shape but do not cover recursive/dynamic imports.
audit.rationale: The policy is valuable, but non-recursive discovery and a static import/export regex have credible blind spots requiring counterfactual fixtures.
audit.action: In Phase 1, prove nested/dynamic counterexamples and replace the scanner with recursive TypeScript-AST or import-graph enforcement.
audit.validation: focused importBoundary test plus negative nested and dynamic-import fixtures; pnpm check:protocol
